newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-KLEIN LEADS BY ONE SHOT AT LPGA TOUR CHAMPIONSHIP.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-KLEIN LEADS BY ONE SHOT AT LPGA TOUR CHAMPIONSHIP.

text.p: Emilee Klein shot a bogey-free four-under-par 68 Friday to take a one-stroke lead over Juli Inkster after two rounds of the inaugural $700,000 LPGA Tour Championship.
The 22-year-old Klein, who captured her first two career LPGA victories in consecutive weeks in August, moved to seven-under 137. Inkster shot a 70 to stand at 138.
Britain's Laura Davies and Australian rookie Karrie Webb, who are battling for the money title, shot two-under 70s and were tied at five under with Michelle McGann and Penny Hammel, who carded 71s.
Davies leads the LPGA with four wins this season, while McGann has captured three titles.
The 22-year-old Klein opened her second round with back-to-back birdies and collected 14 pars and two more birdies the rest of the way. She saved par at the final hole to maintain the lead.
"I just played really solidly," said Klein, who is wrapping up her second full year on the LPGA Tour. "I putted really well. I have been bogeyless the past two days.

"I have learned over the years that it's better in my case to be shorter (off the tee) and be first hitting into the green," she added. "It puts pressure on them. I'll never hit it as far as Laura and Karrie even if I took steroids."

Inkster is 22nd on the LPGA money list, although she has not won since 1992. She had an up and down round, collecting five birdies and three bogeys. A 20-foot birdie putt at the par-five 15th hole gave her sole possession of second place.
"I played well, drove the ball well and hit irons great," Inkster said. "I did not putt as well as I'd like."
Kelly Robbins was alone at four under after recording her second straight 70.
Hall of Famer Nancy Lopez was tied with two-time defending U.S. Open champion Annika Sorenstam of Sweden and Brandie Burton at three under.
Rookie Mayumi Hirase of Japan, who held the lead entering the round, struggled to a 79 to move to two over after a five-under 67 Thursday.
